solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Position with good view of fighting gave guarding soldier purpose

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stand guard around the soldier, holding him inside
letters that are fighting are thrown into disorder, so the word gave is jumbled

parts.note: a soldier ant is the warrior caste of an ant colony
the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: A soldier guarding a position with a good view gave his fighting comrades purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is an insect, the soldier ant of an ant colony, not a man in uniform; the jumbled letters of 'gave' hold it after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vantage point is a place giving a commanding outlook over the surroundings.

clue.text: Look up rising market prices, principally this speeds up inflation

parts.note: an air is a look or manner, as in 'an air of confidence'

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, so the word up is turned round
principally points to the first letters of market and prices

explanation.surface: An economist looks at rising market prices, the main driver of inflation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' looks economic; the definition means pumping air into a tyre or balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: An air pump forces air into tyres or balls, making them inflate faster.

clue.text: Nippers with zest were running wild!

indicators.note: letters running wild are out of control and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: Small children were running wild with great energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nippers' suggests children, as British slang has it; here it means tools that nip.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweezers are small pincers used for plucking or gripping tiny objects.

clue.text: Leaving without one's award

indicators.note: without means the letter for one is dropped from the word

parts.note: going means leaving, departing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone departs without receiving their honour.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for a medal or decoration.

clue.text: Emotional confusion of OAP in East Enders finale's piercing

indicators.note: the final letter pierces the jumbled letters, going inside them
confusion jumbles the letters of OAP, in and East together
the finale of the word Enders is its last letter

explanation.surface: A pensioner gets emotional over the dramatic EastEnders finale.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in London; an OAP is an old-age pensioner. Here 'East' is fodder, and only the S of 'Enders' goes inside the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate means showing strong feeling, intensely emotional.

clue.text: Cool American beefcake finally gets engaged

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of beefcake

explanation.surface: A cool American hunk finally gets engaged to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' suggests a wedding; here it means occupied, like a phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in use is occupied or busy, as an engaged phone line is.

clue.text: Those people with spectacles have name for satellite

parts.note: them refers to those people
a pair of lenses looks like two round letters O

explanation.surface: People in glasses have a name for a satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite, orbiting the planet.

clue.text: Old racer in TT wearies, collapsing after taking flag

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the flag has been taken in first

parts.note: a jack is a small flag flown on a ship

indicators.note: collapsing breaks the letters down into a new order

explanation.surface: An exhausted rider collapses at the Isle of Man TT after taking the chequered flag.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race, so it reads as a place, but its two letters are part of the anagram fodder. A jack is a ship's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackie Stewart was a Scottish Formula One driver, three times world champion.

clue.text: Essence of a map puzzle is finding exit

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The point of a maze-like map puzzle is to find your way out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit offers a way out, a route by which one can get away.

clue.text: Have same opinion as top grade environmentalist protecting duck

parts.note: A is the highest grade on a report

indicators.note: the environmentalist wraps round the duck to protect it

parts.note: a Green is a campaigner for the environment
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Someone shares a view with an excellent environmentalist who is shielding a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The O (cricket's duck, a zero score) goes inside GREEN between the second E and the N.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree on something is to reach the same view about it as someone else.

clue.text: Press witness hedging question about key last letter

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds something, so the witness word encloses the question

parts.note: to witness something is to see it

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so key then last letter is read backwards

parts.note: E is a musical key
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A journalist presses a witness who is hedging when asked about a key final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it goes with 'question', but it turns the key and the last letter round; the hedging witness takes in the question first.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze is to press or compress something firmly.

clue.text: American duffer's last in rink getting difficult jump

indicators.note: the final letter of the word rink is taken

parts.note: a lutz is a demanding figure-skating jump

explanation.surface: A clumsy American skater ends up in the rink attempting a tricky leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Klutz is US slang for a clumsy, inept person, a bungler.

clue.text: Quiet when Twitter's not working!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an order to be silent, stop talking
second meaning: a bird, a twitterer, has stopped its piping and is down

explanation.walkthrough: Twitter looks like the social network; here it is a songbird whose piping is down, out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal command telling someone to be silent or less noisy.

clue.text: Recklessness gets rogue, lacking in respect, regularly nicked

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal or rogue
rude means impolite, lacking respect

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of nicked, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A disrespectful rogue is routinely arrested for reckless behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is a lack of caution, rash or unwise conduct.

clue.text: Investigation of mine accident concealed by authority

indicators.note: the jumbled word is hidden inside the authority

parts.note: an authority on a subject is an expert

indicators.note: an accident makes a mess of things, so the word mine is scrambled

explanation.surface: An expert's inquiry into a mining accident is being hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine accident' reads as a pit disaster; here 'accident' only signals that the letters of 'mine' are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An experiment is a scientific test carried out to discover something.

clue.text: Disengage from Uruguay National Party

parts.note: U is the international vehicle code for Uruguay
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone breaks away from a Uruguayan political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Uruguay's National Party is real, which makes it read as one name rather than three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a catch or fastening is to release or unfasten it.

clue.text: Second year doctor with stomach ache, heading off, is significant

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, is taken off the stomach ache

parts.note: colic is severe abdominal pain

explanation.surface: A second-year doctor suffering from stomach pains has a significant problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbolic means acting as a sign or emblem, carrying meaning beyond itself.

clue.text: Filling in burrito's honestly rubbish

indicators.note: the answer forms the filling inside these words, spanning their join

explanation.surface: Someone frankly declares the filling of a burrito is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Dried fruit and nut salad surprisingly left by daughter

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected arrangement of the letters
the daughter leaves, so her letter is removed from salad

explanation.surface: A daughter has left behind a dried fruit and nut salad, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by daughter' removes D from SALAD to give SALA, which joins NUT for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a seedless raisin, a dried grape.

clue.text: Fairly certain moving upset Terry

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is fairly sure that a moving scene upset Terry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'moving' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pretty sure means confident though not completely so.

clue.text: Social climber gets high with famous model

parts.note: up means high
a star is a famous person
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: A social climber gets a buzz from mingling with a celebrity model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'famous model' reads as one person but splits: STAR, and T for the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves arrogantly.

clue.text: Correctly moreover, describing Duke as wealthy

parts.note: doing something well is doing it correctly

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the word encircles the duke

parts.note: too means also, moreover

explanation.surface: Someone rightly adds that the Duke is a rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of tracing around, putting D inside TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do people are comfortably off, affluent.

clue.text: Stigma around Artificial Intelligence is explosive

indicators.note: the explosive goes around the letters for artificial intelligence

parts.note: TNT is a high explosive

explanation.surface: The stigma attached to artificial intelligence is an explosive issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a mark of disgrace or corruption, a stain on reputation.

clue.text: When in charge, going by book's essential

indicators.note: the book letter goes beside the other pieces, just ahead of them

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: When you are in charge, following the rulebook is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going by book' reads as following the rules; here it puts the book's letter alongside the rest, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental, forming the essential foundation of something.

clue.text: Disease caused by hole in intestine

indicators.note: the hole is placed in the intestine word

parts.note: the gut is the intestine
O is round like a hole

explanation.surface: A medical note says an illness was caused by a perforated bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gout is a joint disease caused by uric acid crystals, often in the big toe.

clue.text: Put in order again for proper gin cocktail

parts.note: real means genuine, proper

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: A bartender tidies the bar again in readiness for a proper gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring things back into line or arrangement.

clue.text: Clipped cat reversing and hit parking light

indicators.note: reversing means the shortened cat is read backwards
clipping cuts off the end, so the last letter of the cat goes

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
to lam is to beat or thrash
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A cat with a trimmed coat backs up and knocks into a parking light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' suggests a groomed coat, but it cuts the last letter off the big cat before it is turned round. To lam is old slang for beating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil lamp is a source of light burning oil through a wick.

clue.text: Genuineness of gold in those days originally tested in financial district

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
then means at that time, in those days

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Gold's purity was once first checked in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of 'tested' and 'in', giving TI. The City is London's financial district, the 'Square Mile'.
explanation.definitionFit: Authenticity is the quality of being real or of undisputed origin.
